rv.q: This unpredictable, well-acted thriller is a great choice for the Halloween season.

Elaine and her husband John Wheeler live in a luxurious townhouse, directly across from another large, but abandoned, building that’s in a state of disrepair. The old house appears to be deserted; however, one night Elaine notices a light shining through one of the windows, revealing a gruesome sight.

Theatergoers interested in seeing an old-school staged thriller (written by the author of the immortal Sorry, Wrong Number) may find some elements to enjoy in this revival. But, unfortunately, this production ultimately falls flat. I am more hopeful for the rest of Raven’s season.

cn.t: This 70s thriller delivers mystery and misdirection with strong performances, though its Rear Window-inspired premise about a woman obsessed with a disturbing sight across the street proves more engaging than groundbreaking.
